name: Nvidia
what: Designs the chips and software most AI models are trained and run on.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (May–Jul 2026)
current.detail: Data center revenue $89.0B, up 117%. Gross margin 75%.

future.label: Company outlook, next quarter
future.detail: Plus or minus 2%. Assumes no data-center sales to China.

drivers: Cloud giants and AI labs racing to build data centers
Each new chip generation sells at higher prices
CUDA software keeps developers on Nvidia hardware
risks: A few huge customers buy most of its chips
Export limits to China
Any slowdown in AI spending would hit fast
Very high expectations are already in the stock price
why: Every major tech company is racing to build AI data centers, and most AI models are trained and run on Nvidia chips. Demand has outrun supply, so Nvidia can charge premium prices: it keeps about 75 cents of every revenue dollar as gross profit. Its CUDA software makes switching to another chipmaker slow and costly.

company: Next quarter revenue of about $108B, up from $96.2B
Management has pointed to about $1 trillion of Blackwell and Rubin chip revenue visibility across 2025–2027
analysts: In June 2026, analysts expected growth of roughly 70% a year through the end of fiscal 2027
They estimated $103B for the current quarter; Nvidia then guided higher, to $108B

scenarios.bull: AI spending keeps accelerating, new Rubin chips sell at even higher prices, and China reopens as extra upside.
scenarios.base: Growth slows from triple digits as comparisons get tougher, but stays strong while data-center building continues.
scenarios.bear: Big customers cut spending or shift to their own chips, and margins fall from their peak.

name: Micron Technology
what: Makes memory chips (DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory) that every AI server needs.

past.label: Fiscal 2026 revenue (year to Aug 2026)
past.detail: Up from $37.4B in fiscal 2025, about 3.6 times larger.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (Jun–Aug 2026)
current.detail: Versus $11.3B a year earlier. Gross margin 86.8%.

drivers: AI servers need far more high-bandwidth memory
Tight memory supply lets prices rise
Only three big memory makers worldwide
risks: Memory is famously cyclical: booms are followed by price crashes
Samsung and SK hynix are adding capacity
Margins this high rarely last
why: AI servers need huge amounts of high-bandwidth memory, and only three companies make it at scale: Micron, Samsung and SK hynix. Supply is tight, so memory prices have soared. That pushed Micron's gross margin to 86.8% last quarter, extraordinary for a memory company.

company: Next quarter revenue of about $61.5B, plus or minus $1.5B, up from $54.2B
analysts: Analysts debate how long the memory upcycle lasts: past booms ended when new factories came online and prices fell

scenarios.bull: AI demand keeps memory scarce into 2027 and beyond, and margins stay near record highs.
scenarios.base: Growth continues but slows as competitors' new capacity arrives and prices level off.
scenarios.bear: Supply catches up, memory prices fall fast, and profits drop sharply, as in past memory busts.

name: Microsoft
what: Sells cloud computing (Azure), Office and Windows software, LinkedIn and Xbox.

past.label: Azure revenue, same quarter last year
past.detail: Azure is Microsoft's cloud business, where most AI demand lands.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (Jul–Sep 2026)
current.detail: Azure $33.2B, up 48%. Microsoft Cloud $63.9B, up 30%. Operating income up 21%.

future.label: Capital spending this quarter
future.detail: Up from $19.4B a year earlier: a large bet on future AI demand.

drivers: Companies moving work to the cloud
AI tools built into Office and Azure
Recurring subscription revenue
risks: Huge data-center spending must pay off
Competition from Amazon and Google
Regulation of AI and big tech
why: Businesses keep moving their computing to the cloud, and AI is speeding that up. Azure grew 48% last quarter, and Microsoft's CFO says customer demand still exceeds the capacity it can supply. Its commercial backlog, contracts signed but not yet delivered, reached $677B, up 73%.

company: December-quarter revenue of $96B to $97.1B, up from $92.3B
Capital spending roughly doubled from a year ago to add data-center capacity
analysts: The key debate: whether the AI spending pays back with enough profit to keep margins high

scenarios.bull: AI services become a large, high-margin business on top of steady software subscriptions.
scenarios.base: Steady high-teens growth, with margins pressured somewhat by data-center costs.
scenarios.bear: AI demand cools after heavy spending, leaving costly unused capacity.

name: Eli Lilly
what: Pharmaceutical company behind Mounjaro and Zepbound, leading diabetes and obesity medicines.
drivers: Demand for obesity and diabetes drugs
New pill versions and new uses for existing drugs
An aging, heavier world population
risks: Drug price pressure from governments
Competition from Novo Nordisk and new entrants
Trial results and safety findings
why: Mounjaro and Zepbound, Lilly's diabetes and weight-loss medicines, are among the fastest-selling drugs ever. Together they brought in about $16B last quarter. Obesity affects hundreds of millions of people, and these drugs work better than anything before them.

analysts: In January 2026, Leerink projected $94.3B in revenue by 2027; Lilly's own 2026 guidance is already close to that path
Truist sees combined peak sales of its obesity drugs, including the oral pill orforglipron, reaching $101B a year

scenarios.bull: Oral obesity pills widen the market, Medicare coverage expands, and new drugs like retatrutide add another leg of growth.
scenarios.base: Strong growth continues, with prices gradually falling as competition and government pressure increase.
scenarios.bear: Competitors match its results, prices drop sharply, or trials disappoint.

name: Costco
what: Membership warehouse retailer that earns much of its profit from membership fees.

current.label: Fiscal 2026 net sales (year to Aug 2026)
current.detail: Q4 comparable sales up 9.4%. 84.1 million paid members, 92.3% renewal in the US and Canada.

future.label: Membership fees, latest quarter
future.detail: Up 7.3%. Recurring, high-margin income that funds low prices.

drivers: Very loyal members
Low prices that win share in any economy
New warehouses, including abroad
risks: Stock usually trades at a high valuation
Thin margins on goods
Consumer spending slowdowns
why: Costco earns loyalty through low prices and makes much of its profit from membership fees, which 92% of US and Canadian members renew. Sales grew 10.1% in fiscal 2026, and its 3.0% net margin was the highest in ten years. Higher gas prices added about 3% to sales, a boost that may not last.

company: Plans to open 33 warehouses in fiscal 2027, up from 28 in fiscal 2026
analysts: Consensus expects sales growth of about 7.5% and profit growth of about 9.6% across fiscal 2027–2028
The stock trades at about 45 times last year's earnings, a high price for steady growth

scenarios.bull: International expansion and digital sales speed up growth, and members keep renewing at record rates.
scenarios.base: Steady high-single-digit growth, the reliable compounding it is known for.
scenarios.bear: Growth slows to normal retail levels and its high valuation shrinks.

name: GE Vernova
what: Builds gas turbines, wind turbines and grid equipment that generate and move electricity.

past.label: Orders, latest quarter
past.detail: Up 96% organically: demand is running far ahead of what it can ship.

future.label: Backlog of orders
future.detail: 2026 revenue guidance raised to $46.5–47.5B; free cash flow guidance $16–17B.

drivers: Electricity demand from data centers and factories
Aging grids that need replacing
Long waiting lists for turbines
risks: Wind business has struggled
Project delays and cost overruns
Demand forecasts could prove too high
why: Electricity demand is rising for the first time in decades because of data centers, factories and electrification. Utilities need gas turbines and grid equipment, and GE Vernova has years of orders waiting: orders nearly doubled last quarter and its backlog is $197B.

company: 2026 revenue guidance of $46.5–47.5B, raised in October
2028 targets set in December 2025: about $52B revenue, a 20% adjusted EBITDA margin and about $200B backlog. The backlog is already near that target.
analysts: UBS called the 2028 targets a very strong update when they were raised

scenarios.bull: Power demand keeps rising faster than expected, and long order queues let it raise prices.
scenarios.base: It works through its backlog with steady growth and improving margins.
scenarios.bear: Data-center building slows, orders are delayed or cancelled, and the wind business keeps losing money.

name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC)
what: Manufactures the most advanced chips in the world for other companies, including the AI chips designed by Nvidia and others.

past.label: Net income a year earlier (Jul–Sep 2025)
past.detail: Profit grew 68.7% to NT$763.1B in the latest quarter.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (Jul–Sep 2026)
current.detail: Up 50.9% in Taiwan dollars. Gross margin 66.4%; 7-nanometer and more advanced chips were 79% of wafer revenue.

future.label: Q4 2026 revenue guidance
future.detail: Company guidance: gross margin 65–67%, operating margin 56.5–58.5%, as its 2-nanometer technology ramps up.

drivers: Demand for AI chips from data centers
The shift to 2- and 3-nanometer manufacturing
Very high margins on leading-edge production
risks: Geopolitical tension around Taiwan
Dependence on a few large customers such as Nvidia
Huge spending needed to stay ahead; currency swings affect reported results
watch: Share of revenue from the newest nodes
Gross margin as new factories open
why: Almost every advanced AI chip, whoever designs it, is made in TSMC's factories, so it earns from the AI build-out no matter which chip designer wins. Demand for its newest processes is running ahead of what it can produce, which lets it keep margins near two-thirds of revenue: 7-nanometer and newer technologies were 79% of wafer revenue last quarter.

company: Q4 2026 revenue of US$52.3–54.3B with a 65–67% gross margin (Oct 15, 2026)
Full-year 2026 revenue growth of about 44% in US dollars, raised from slightly above 40% in July
2026 capital spending of US$60–64B, with 2026–2028 spending significantly higher than the previous three years
analysts: Q3 profit came in slightly ahead of analyst estimates compiled by LSEG (Oct 15, 2026)
Futurum Group said the Q4 guidance midpoint was ahead of prior Street expectations (Oct 20, 2026)

scenarios.bull: AI demand keeps outrunning supply, the 2-nanometer ramp goes smoothly and margins stay near record levels.
scenarios.base: Revenue keeps growing with AI spending while heavy factory investment and new overseas plants trim margins slightly.
scenarios.bear: Big customers cut AI chip orders, tension around Taiwan disrupts operations or trade, or new factories cost more than planned.

name: Sony Group
what: Owns PlayStation, one of the world's largest music companies, a Hollywood film and TV studio, and the leading maker of camera image sensors.

past.label: Operating income, Jul–Sep 2025
past.detail: Rose 45% to ¥622.3B in the latest quarter; operating margin went from 13.8% to 18.1%.

current.label: Latest quarter sales (Jul–Sep 2026)
current.detail: Up about 4% at constant exchange rates. Net income rose 44% to ¥449.6B. Pictures sales rose 48% and games operating income 83%.

future.label: FY2026 operating income forecast (year to March 2027)
future.detail: Company forecast raised Nov 5 from ¥1.72T; sales forecast raised to ¥13.0T from ¥12.5T, with a 35-yen dividend, up 10 yen.

drivers: PlayStation games and network services
Film and TV hits in Pictures
Music streaming
A weak yen that lifts overseas earnings in yen
risks: About 6 points of the 10% sales growth came from the weak yen and would reverse if it strengthens
Image sensor sales fell 6% on weaker smartphone demand
Film results depend on hits and swing year to year
Changing US tariff policy on hardware
watch: Game segment profit as the console ages
Image sensor sales to phone makers
Results against the raised full-year forecast
why: Sony has turned into an entertainment company that makes money from the content people return to: games, music catalogs, films and shows, sold digitally at high margins. In the July–September quarter games operating income rose 83% and Pictures sales 48%, and the company raised its full-year profit forecast by 9%. A weak yen helps: the dollar averaged 159.3 yen in the quarter versus 147.4 a year earlier, which inflates overseas earnings when counted in yen.

company: FY2026 sales of ¥13.0T, operating income ¥1.87T and net income ¥1.33T, all raised on Nov 5, 2026
Image sensor sales essentially flat for the year at ¥2.12T, with operating income forecast raised to ¥450B
Forecast assumes about 153 yen per dollar for the rest of the year, below the quarter's 159.3 average
analysts: Zacks attributed the quarter's sales growth to gaming and Pictures strength (Nov 5, 2026)

scenarios.bull: Games and music keep growing digital sales at high margins, Pictures has more hits, and sensor demand from phone makers recovers.
scenarios.base: Entertainment keeps growing while sensors stay flat, and the raised forecast is roughly met.
scenarios.bear: The yen strengthens and shrinks overseas earnings, console sales fade, and smartphone sensor demand keeps falling.

sources.name: Sony Group Q2 FY2026 results presentation (SEC Form 6-K), Nov 5, 2026

name: Richemont
what: Owns Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels and Buccellati jewelry and watchmakers including IWC, Jaeger-LeCoultre and Vacheron Constantin.

current.label: Sales, six months to Sep 2026
current.detail: Up 17% at constant exchange rates. Operating profit rose 33% to €3.13B (25.5% margin; 23.6% excluding €229M of one-time tariff-related gains). Jewelry sales rose 19% at constant rates with a 35.3% margin.

future.label: Company outlook
future.detail: The chairman expects the environment to remain volatile for the foreseeable future and says the watch recovery is unlikely to be linear. Net cash stood at €7.73B.

drivers: Jewelry demand at Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels
Sales through its own stores, now 78% of the total
Americas sales up 23% and Japan up 30% at constant rates
Price increases that mostly offset higher gold costs
risks: High gold prices squeeze gross margin; excluding the tariff item, gross margin fell 0.7 points
Growth slowed to 13% in the second quarter from 20% in the first
Middle East and Africa sales fell 2% amid the regional conflict
Watch demand in China remains soft
Currency hedging losses of €418M outweighed €316M of currency gains
watch: Gross margin as gold prices move
Spending by Chinese and Middle East shoppers
why: Richemont is a jewelry business more than a watch business, and jewelry is where luxury demand is strongest: its jewelry houses grew sales 19% at constant rates and earned a 35.3% operating margin, against 8.8% at the watchmakers. Selling mostly through its own stores (72% retail, 6% online) gives it control over pricing, which let it raise prices enough to mostly offset the higher cost of gold. Operating cash flow rose 35% to €2.5B.

company: No numeric forecast; management expects a volatile environment for the foreseeable future (Nov 13, 2026)
Watchmaker recovery described as unlikely to be linear, with soft demand in China (Nov 13, 2026)
analysts: Shares opened more than 4% lower on Nov 13, 2026 even though first-half net profit beat forecasts (Yahoo Finance)

scenarios.bull: Jewelry keeps growing in the double digits, price increases keep pace with gold, and watch demand in China recovers.
scenarios.base: Jewelry growth slows toward the second-quarter pace while watches improve gradually and margins hold.
scenarios.bear: Gold keeps rising faster than prices can follow, wealthy shoppers in China and the Gulf pull back, and growth slows further.

sources.name: Richemont, results for the six months ended 30 September 2026, Nov 13, 2026
Yahoo Finance, Stock market today, Nov 13, 2026
